# Workflow completion performance review

Owner: `/root/m1_optimizations`, dedicated performance reviewer,
GPT-6.1-sol / max, 2026-10-09. This increment owns only this review file and
explicitly agreed safe temporary probes. Implementation owners fix their own
code; root owns shared policy, milestone integration, commits and pushes.

## Contract published before dependent suggestions

Read current `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/CONTINUE.md`, completion coordination,
architecture, ordered implementation plan, transport contract, Raft/storage
design and the actual prior O1/O2 review. Remaining M1 and every later milestone
need separate performance/resource review. Performance evidence supplements
preserved source scenarios, semantic/model tests and real fault gates; it never
turns incomplete, ignored or unexecuted source cases into passing parity.

The latest completion scope includes required governance, approvals, budgets,
durable effects and durable steps. Older conditional breadth deferral cannot
omit them; unrelated product or Elixir-specific cases require explicit per-case
dispositions from the source/parity owner. Resource profiles preserve required
assertions rather than silently lowering their accepted sizes or item counts.

Preserve pure synchronous domain boundaries, deterministic committed bytes and
decisions, value identity, full canonical record equality, exact FIFO/due order,
explicit continuation, borrowed input preservation, checked arithmetic and
reported fallible boundaries. Host allocation/storage failure is recovery/retry
or replica failure, never a durable deterministic business rejection. Do not
clone a whole partition, move effects inward, weaken validation for speed or
replace private/public vectors indiscriminately. API/ownership changes require
published owner contracts and reciprocal review before dependent implementation.

Each review records actual inspected paths, proposed change, existing semantic
tests, resource/cost hypothesis, measurements and limits, owner response, and
independent recheck. No claim of independent review without reading the actual
peer file/code or executing the stated check. Reviewers communicate directly
with domain, architecture and root; no interruptions or peer edits.

## Resource and performance acceptance by milestone

These are proposed review gates grounded in the existing architecture and
ordered plan, not claims of completed implementation or new public limits.
Numerical operation limits need source/compatibility review and owner agreement;
local deployment settings cannot cause different replicated apply decisions.

| Milestone | Required resource/correctness evidence | Focused measurements after APIs stabilize |
|---|---|---|
| M1 pure domain | Count **and byte/work** bounds on admitted values, policy collections, batch writes, retained outcomes and canonical encoding; unchanged input on rejection; complete group-local validation before output; explicit replay/conflict/time rules; checked overflow and no allocation-error business outcome | Handle layouts, retained capacities, copied bytes and reducer mixtures; maximum admitted batch/record/policy sizes; empty/binary/absent cases; equal distinct canonical snapshots; same outputs across supported platforms and model replay |
| M2 persistence | Real atomic records/indexes/history/outcome/time/checkpoint transaction; vote/log durability separate; every acknowledged fault hook actually reached; no success from memory; bounded snapshot capture/staging/rebuild; uncertain commit reconciled before reuse | Durable transaction and log completion latency, bytes written/read and write amplification, batch-delay tradeoff, restart/replay and snapshot duration/peak retained bytes under concurrent apply; no relaxed durability benchmark counted as equivalent |
| M3 consensus | Three-node minority/failover/restart/snapshot tests, successful outcome preservation, current-leader strong-read barrier, ordered apply and bounded replication queues; client saturation cannot starve peer progress | Offered versus committed/applied/answered rates, commit-to-apply lag, log/snapshot queue bytes, replication backlog, heartbeat/election progress and recovery time with disk stalls, leader loss and skewed groups |
| M4 application, HTTP/TCP, worker | One shared tenant/group/byte/work admission owner, bounded ingress/decode/waiters, whole-response reservation before proposal, permit ownership through underlying submitted completion, unknown-outcome replay across transports, guarded worker execution and graceful drain | Both transports separately and mixed with identical durability/consistency/payload settings; intended-arrival and actual-send latency, rejection/unknown fractions, retained input/output capacities and RSS, slow readers/bodies, timeout/disconnect races and maintenance reserve |
| M5 workflow breadth | Bounded signals/schedules/fanout/children, policy, governance/approval/budget/effect/step operations, same-group atomicity, every required source assertion and parent accounting; cancellation/completion and signal/timeout races | Work/copies versus child and touched-record counts, scheduling/index update cost, maximum supported fanout, policy resolution mixtures and retained event/outcome growth; no hidden full-group clone |
| M6 queries/projections | Authority decides correctness; coherent watermark/incorporation, rebuild from durable events, bounded page bytes/count/work, cursor scope and no unbounded pinned transaction | Strong/projected point and range profiles separately; lag/rebuild rate and retained bytes, query/index write amplification, maximum pages and filters, cold cache and concurrent writes; full result materialization is measured/rejected before exposure |
| M7 retention/operations | Cleanup cannot remove reachable bytes, live accounting or promised outcomes/history; explicit expired versus not-observed evidence, safe backup/restore/fence identities, bounded background budgets | Retained bytes per workflow/outcome/event, cleanup throughput/pause and foreground interference, backup/restore duration and staging peak, capacity exhaustion/recovery and rolling-upgrade behavior |
| M8 performance/cache | All predecessor semantics hold with cache absent/cold/evicted/rebuilt; cache never validates leases/FIFO/auth; approved safe boundary and supported platform/feature matrix | Reproducible mixed offered-load capacity and tails, contention/concurrency evidence, memory overhead and cache hit/miss/rebuild distributions; reuse only when measured benefit justifies complexity |

An M1 local cost probe can support an optimization decision without claiming a
service SLO. M2/M3 faults precede runtime throughput claims. The existing
operations design's healthy small-request p99 target is **unvalidated** and
conditional on its workload/topology/load envelope; no unconditional latency
gate or guarantee is introduced here.

## Measurement and probe discipline

Use the pinned compiler, locked/offline builds, isolated targets and approved
temporary project/data paths; no new dependencies, unsafe, policy suppressions
or production edits by this reviewer. Record revision/file hashes, compiler,
target, optimization settings, allocator/backend/durability options, hardware,
payload/record/policy distributions, run count, sample size and raw output.
Keep construction/drop, preparation, decision, persistence and serialization
costs separately identifiable. Compare semantically equal variants using the
same admitted inputs; keep public Vec constructors/slice accessors when the
proposal concerns only private immutable representation.

Do not time expensive probes amid uncontrolled concurrent builds. Agree an idle
measurement window with root once the relevant API is stable. Repeat baseline
and candidate in that window with warmup, alternating order and retained raw
samples; report variation and ambiguous results. Structural layout/count/byte
probes and ordinary semantic tests can run earlier. No allocator-call or RSS
claim from handle size, address reuse or elapsed nanoseconds alone. Use safe
capacity/length/work counters first; any external profiling tool must have its
own approved scope and reproducible configuration.

Runtime load tests use an offered-arrival schedule that continues during stalls,
record intended-arrival-to-outcome and actual-send-to-outcome separately, and
account for every offered attempt: applied, durable rejection, not-submitted,
unknown, timeout and unavailable. Publish p50/p95/p99/p99.9 with sample counts,
offered/completed rates, rejection fraction, backlog and memory high-water marks.
Do not discard failed attempts, saturate histogram outliers or apply two
coordinated-omission corrections. Retries preserve original intent/scope and
remain distinguishable from independent operations. Faults must be observed at
acknowledged hooks, rather than inferred from a delay or process exit.

## Initial actual-code findings and remaining M1 questions

**P-C1 — row budgets are not byte-cost certificates.** Read current
`wf-domain/src/claim/{request,index,selection}.rs`. Selection bounds are 1,000
outputs, 16,384 candidates and 4,096 direct heads; the filter footprint is 64.
Canonical equality compares complete record values and key comparisons use
opaque bytes. Prefix/head sorting and coherence therefore still scale with
admitted key/record bytes, even when row counts are fixed. Current payload
admission is an explicit remaining M1 gap. Request: domain/architecture publish
the byte/work admission contract before describing runtime selection as
resource-bounded. Do not replace full equality with address, ID or version
acceptance. Future canonical-ID index rows need their own API/invariant review.

**P-C2 — reducer ownership has measurable clone costs.** Actual
`workflow/{create_claim,lifecycle,retry_transition,plan}.rs` preserves borrowed
inputs by cloning records/command fields and copying history state/worker bytes.
Clone-then-replace can copy an old payload that is immediately overwritten.
This is a cost hypothesis for actual reducer-mixture probes, not permission to
mutate inputs or box every record field. Publish whether a new batch plan owns
bounded final records, borrowed deltas or another reviewed representation; never
turn it into a whole-partition clone. Broad boxing and the prior O4 borrowed
retry-target overlay remain **unaccepted** until an owner chooses and validates
them with actual final APIs and retained semantics.

**P-C3 — explicit fallible sites do not cover all allocation.** Actual
PartitionKey construction uses checked sizing and `try_reserve_exact`; claim
frontier/result vectors use fallible reservation. Record/policy clones and
ordered-set/map insertions remain allocation paths. A future resource contract
must say which errors are reported and which host failures abort/recover; it
cannot persist an allocator-dependent result as a replicated business outcome.
Keep PartitionKey's growable/fallible Vec storage unless finishing/shrinking
semantics are explicitly reviewed. Bound accepted lengths before expensive
copying/encoding, and distinguish logical lengths from retained capacities.

**P-C4 — canonical encoding/replay must bound both work and retained data.**
Architecture requires canonical client intent distinct from prepared entry,
dedup before changed guards, meaningful batch order, opaque bytes, independent
versions and exact accepted/rejected outcomes. Domain/architecture proposals
should identify maximum encoded bytes/touched records, duplicate-field/default
normalization, fallible builder behavior and replay retention ownership.
Do not use Rust object layout, randomized hash iteration or transient allocation
addresses as committed encoding/identity. Streaming a digest can be evaluated
only after exact versioned byte vectors are frozen; it cannot alter semantics.

Owner responses and actual new API/code review are pending at publication.
Domain and architecture were directly notified of this scope; root was notified
that no timed probe will run before stable APIs and an agreed measurement window.

## Carried evidence and current external checks

Prior [O1/O2 review](workflow-m1-optimizations.md) is closed: private RecordId and
LeaseToken boxes plus stack decimal formatting preserved constructors/accessors,
binary bytes, checked partition sizing and all 99 retained type/domain tests.
Its local aarch64 handle reductions and partition medians are historical focused
evidence, not a new run or service/RSS/clone-speed guarantee. Broad record and
PartitionKey boxing, canonical-ID index redesign and O4 remain deferred.

Rechecked primary documentation on 2026-10-09 before extending runtime measurement
contracts. Rust's [Vec guarantees/conversion](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.into_boxed_slice)
distinguish length/capacity and possible shrinking during boxed conversion;
exact length/capacity can convert without reallocation. This supports measuring
conversion and retained capacity separately. Current stable docs show Rust
1.99.0; this does not create a new toolchain or API requirement.

[Tokio spawn_blocking](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/task/fn.spawn_blocking.html)
documents queued work and that started blocking tasks cannot be aborted;
[Tokio timeout](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/time/fn.timeout.html)
can be exceeded by work that does not yield. Runtime review will therefore
check ownership of permits/buffers through underlying work, not just the caller's
waiting future. These are discovery checks, not selected runtime dependencies.

[HdrHistogram correction](https://docs.rs/hdrhistogram/latest/hdrhistogram/struct.Histogram.html#method.record_correct)
adds interval-based synthetic samples; at-recording and post-correction are
mutually exclusive. Saturating recording can hide extremes. Keep raw outcomes,
overflow and any correction assumptions explicit; correction cannot supply
missing failed requests or replace the offered-load schedule.

No new performance probe, production change, benchmark, fault experiment or
TDD cycle is claimed in this initial contract publication. Remaining acceptance
gates are real work for their implementation milestones. Dedicated review will
continue through root follow-ups after this finite initial review completes.

## Independent peer contract review and source-limit evidence

Actually read `workflow-completion-domain.md` and
`workflow-completion-architecture.md` after both owners published their initial
contracts. A-M1-01..05 preserve distinct identity/admission, full typed policy
installation, coherent group-local batches, explicit time/prepared inputs and
request replay. Domain proposes borrowing exact versioned retained outcome bytes
before current guards and returning bounded owned touched-record plans. These
are appropriate initial ownership contracts; no record boxing, canonical
weakening or whole-partition clone is proposed. Actual production API/tests are
not published at this read, so implementation acceptance remains pending.

**P-M1-01 — actual encoded bytes, immutable limits.** Architecture relayed the
domain owner's explicit acceptance of A-C2: admission takes actual borrowed
encoded key/value slices and derives `.len()`, rather than trusting claimed
lengths. This is the required contract at the pure apply boundary; outer codecs
remain responsible for producing verified versioned bytes. New decoded wire
limits are additional edge policy, not a replacement for source apply limits.
Retained original record bytes must also be bounded before cloning to a plan.

Independently checked the isolated baseline is source-clean at the exact pinned
commit, then read `raft/apply_context.ex:1-170`, complete `raft/apply_limits.ex`,
complete `flow/storage_scope.ex`, `flow/system_metadata.ex:1-210`,
`flow/mutation_attrs.ex:1-172`, complete `flow/policy_patch.ex` and relevant
`flow/retry_policy.ex` normalization/snapshot routines. Actual distinctions:

- Versioned ApplyContext is replicated state, rather than live process settings.
  Its default flow batch is **1,000**, hard maximum **100,000**; default value
  size **1 MiB**, hard maximum **512 MiB**. ApplyLimits consumes `records` and
  `children` from one combined item budget. Those maxima are source observations,
  not a recommendation to allocate a maximum batch times maximum value.
- StorageScope's physical isolation scope is **8 KiB**; SystemMetadata has
  **16 fields**, **8 KiB encoded** metadata and **4 KiB** keyword values. Logical
  partition bytes, full composed keys and physical isolation encoding are
  different admission objects. Binary identity cannot be text-normalized.
- RetryPolicy validates the **final normalized policy** using external encoded
  size, with a **256 KiB** snapshot limit; snapshot batch has a separate **4 MiB**
  limit and encoded policy allows **1 KiB** envelope overhead. PolicyPatch
  recursively merges existing state/backoff fields and deletes explicit null
  states. A small incoming patch can retain a large old definition.

**P-M1-02 — final policy/output bounds.** Request to domain: validate final
merged policy bytes/counts and aggregate plans/outcome sizes, rather than only
incoming patch bytes or per-value sizes. Source encoded limits cannot be
certified by summing raw typed field lengths without the exact outer encoding.
A no-copy preview/length pass is an optimization option after merge semantics
are frozen; it must retain deletion, defaults, replace/patch and generation CAS.
No implementation or throughput improvement is claimed.

**P-M1-03 — replay borrows need a durable outer owner.** Returning borrowed
original outcome bytes avoids duplicating the stored outcome inside the domain
decision. Their authoritative view lifetime must cover consumption, or an outer
owner must copy/retain bounded bytes with a charged reservation before releasing
the view. A transport waiter ending cannot release a submitted operation's
authority/output ownership. The pure domain API need not import runtime,
storage guards, shared reference counting or async to satisfy this.

**P-M1-04 — bounded sequential/atomic work.** Unique scoped identities and
group placement are checked before building owned touched plans; late failures
return no partial plan. Where source semantics need sequential overlays, bound
the overlay to touched records and preserve caller order. A complete authority
map may be borrowed, but scans/copies must not grow with unrelated partition
records. Aggregate copied/encoded bytes and touched cardinality are distinct
from input count; both are measured once actual APIs are stable.

Read the actual selected `transports/intent-digest.md` grammar. Its prefix,
tag/u64 length, byte-sorted unique map keys, caller list order and absent/null/
empty distinctions are explicit. **P-M1-05 — stream only the same grammar:**
checked length/depth/item pass followed by safe incremental hash updates can
avoid an extra whole-request byte buffer. This is already a permitted design
option, not a new format or a second normalization path. Map ordering work
remains bounded and exact independent vectors must establish equivalence.
Domain receives validated fixed digest/version/prepared values; application
owns typed client-intent production. No hashing dependency is requested here.

Concrete findings and these source limits were sent directly to domain,
architecture and root. Architecture actually read the full performance note
and agreed with P-C1..04, immutable actual byte slices, full canonical equality,
bounded touched plans, operational allocation failure and retention separate
from caller waiting. It highlighted future bounded pinned MVCC view lifetime
and a bounded blocking-worker queue as adapter measurements; those backend
facts remain its primary-documentation research until separately verified by
this reviewer. Its response is independently attributed, not an adapter test.

Initial contract review found no architecture/ownership blocker in the published
proposals. Final API/semantic/resource rechecks and the pending time ADR are
required before M1 acceptance. Root will assign stable milestone code and agree
temporary probe scope; no new probe or timed measurement was run in this review.

## ADR-004 and first actual implementation review

Independently read the full root-owned ADR-004 and current scope/time/position
types plus new scope/time and group-batch tests. Selected namespace caps remain
separate from complete encoded scope/key limits. Group/recovery/request caps and
the default **16 MiB** aggregate are explicit new resource choices; source value
and batch hard maxima and ordinary network caps remain distinct. The initial
unselected **64 MiB** hard aggregate ceiling was removed by the domain owner
after root review; actual positive larger aggregate profiles require outer
resource review and checked sums. No new source acceptance size is inferred.

The HLC lexicographic maximum and independent wall maximum use bounded scalar
work. For valid pairs, their combined maximum wall remains at most the maximum
physical component, so advancing the pair preserves `CommittedTime` validity.
No allocator/clock effect is needed. Architecture later caught A-T1 in the
control implementation: execution used wall instead of HLC physical. Actual
root ADR now explicitly selects HLC physical, separately retaining wall context;
current `control.rs` reads that physical component. Its real divergent-clock
RED/green and final implementation review remain separate owner evidence.
The selected time rule does not promise safe physical-time leases without the
later skew/leader-change/tick adapter gates.

Read actual `workflow/admission.rs` and `workflow/batch.rs`: borrowed actual
command/key/value bytes are summed with checked arithmetic; placement and
duplicate IDs validate before plans; touched canonical record bytes are charged
before reducer clones; invalid authority and local allocation errors remain
`ApplyError`, while immutable admission rejection returns no partial plan.
This resolves the initial tiny-command/large-current-record concern in P-M1-04.
Output/history/fixed per-item amplification still needs a conservative stable
rule and final tests; `size_of`/target layout must never decide a replicated
business rejection or stand in for wire bytes.

**P-B1 — authoritative retry allocation provenance gap, owner corrected.**
Initial actual preflight omitted `BatchItem.retry_policy`. InstalledRetryPolicy
validated nonempty targets without byte admission; `policy::resolve` copied
type/state exhaustion targets, including ones later overridden, and retry plans
copied the final target into record/history. This permitted an oversized
authoritative policy to escape tiny command/current-record budgets. The finding
was published directly to domain/root/architecture before owner correction.
Domain reports an observed failing regression followed by **5/5** batch green;
those owner logs will be read when published, not claimed as this reviewer's
pre-fix execution. Actual fix borrows/charges only the selected type/logical-state
layers before reduce, with no clone/scan of unrelated state definitions.

## Additional preimplementation findings and peer contracts

**P-P1 — definition validation copies before admission.** Independently read
actual `policy/definition.rs`, `installation.rs` and `install_validation.rs`.
`WorkflowDefinition::new` currently constructs `definition.install_command()`
before `validate_patch`: that call clones the workflow type, every state name
and state patch before checking their count/raw bytes. Requested owner change:
validate borrowed definition fields first, preserving the public materializing
`install_command` API. Also the initial raw-byte accumulator is assigned
`workflow_type.len()` without an immediate maximum check, so a no-byte patch can
pass that helper with an oversized type. Validate the initial type contribution
before any candidate copy. Domain/root were notified directly. At this read,
`prepare_install` remains an explicit preimplementation rejection stub; this is
a concrete pre-GREEN resource finding, not a claimed final install failure.
Check existing authority, patch entry count and exact final unique cardinality
including additions/removals before cloning a candidate. A final encoded cap
does not replace these pre-copy gates. Owner response/actual rerun are pending.

**P-A1 — empty encoded-value occurrences have unbounded work.** Actual
`admit_command` loops every `encoded_values` entry but charges only its byte
length. The decoder correspondence obligation does not yet state or enforce a
finite schema-derived count. Sent domain/root a required cardinality gate or
exact finite trusted codec invariant before that loop. The approved temporary
probe independently observed counts **0 / 1,024 / 65,536**, all empty slices,
each returning **`Ok(6)`** with inline/aggregate limits **64** and batch limit
**1**. The run exited **0**, warning-free, raw log
`/private/tmp/ferricstore2-completion-performance-encoded-count-baseline.log`.
This is actual acceptance/work-input evidence, not a timing, allocation count
or claim that an implemented outer decoder admits these slices. An immutable
finite count/validated codec contract must accompany actual byte admission;
no native layout or invented source byte semantics decide rejection.

Read root's actual normalized-intent contract, full selected grammar, current
private application/commands scaffolds and pinned lock entry `sha2=0.11.0`.
No encoder/hash application dependency is implemented at this read. The
streaming same-grammar proposal has no initial ownership/resource blocker.
Concrete gates sent to root: the complete byte budget includes the 13-byte
prefix, every 9-byte tagged header, list/map count words, encoded map keys and

counts and key bytes before allocating ordering references/uniqueness work;

Independent pre-encoder vectors and boundary cases must distinguish binary

Typed comparison helpers confer no authorization, codec or apply authority;

Relevant reading and concrete lessons:

- [Official Vec guarantees/conversion](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#guarantees)
  and [into_boxed_slice](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.into_boxed_slice):
  length, capacity and live allocation differ; growth can reallocate;
  boxing removes spare capacity, while shrink can move or remain in place.
  Exact reservation gives at least requested capacity. Keep growable builders
  as Vec; preserve fallible reservation and measure actual capacity, not an
  assumed allocator policy.
- [Official Box ownership/layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/boxed/index.html):
  Box owns heap contents and drops them. Its single-pointer Sized guarantee
  does not apply to a slice; our Box-slice handle sizes are local measurements.
  Neither this guarantee nor O5 proves faster cloning of bytes.
- [Official allocation contract](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/alloc/trait.GlobalAlloc.html#the-global_allocator-attribute):
  compiler transformations may remove/merge allocation operations. Source
  call counts, pointer reuse and handle size are not allocator-count proofs.
  No first-party unsafe/custom counting allocator is introduced.
- [Official black_box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/hint/fn.black_box.html):
  obscure inputs and consume results to resist folding/dead work. It is
  best-effort and backend-dependent; it is not a correctness/security boundary.
  Put barriers around inputs before computation, not only a precomputed result.
- [Cargo release profiles](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#release)
  and [rustc codegen options](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/codegen-options/index.html#opt-level):
  benchmark the same pinned release configuration, target and features;
  ordinary Cargo release uses optimization level3. Changing LTO/CPU/codegen
  settings creates a different experiment, not evidence for a representation
  change. Checked arithmetic remains explicit even with release overflow checks.
- [Nicholas Nethercote's Rust Performance Book: benchmarking](https://nnethercote.github.io/perf-book/benchmarking.html)
  and [heap allocation](https://nnethercote.github.io/perf-book/heap-allocations.html):
  select useful metrics and actual workloads, record noisy layout-dependent
  variation, and investigate hot allocation sizes/distributions before choosing
  storage or reservation. Reusing a builder can avoid allocation but retains
  capacity; small-vector alternatives are not guaranteed faster. No extra
  collection dependency or cross-request secret-retaining pool is proposed.
- [Criterion's author documentation: timing loops](https://bheisler.github.io/criterion.rs/book/user_guide/timing_loops.html)
  and [analysis](https://bheisler.github.io/criterion.rs/book/analysis.html):
  distinguish setup/operation/drop costs, bound batches when retaining outputs,
  warm up, retain repeated raw samples/outliers and compare baseline/change
  with variability. Small background changes can produce statistical signals;
  an isolated quiet window and repeated runs remain necessary. Reading its
  methodology does not adopt Criterion or provide its confidence intervals.

through black_box; verify bytes/equality/bounds outside timed loops. Repeat

is justified. It starts empty and reserves one slot per push; a checked complete
tree pass could provide an exact initial segment reservation and bound all
nested ordering work before constructing metadata. Compare tiny/18-vector,
many-key maps, deep nested maps and 1KiB/64KiB/near-limit borrowed payloads.

pass cost can hurt small inputs; reserving the maximum profile for every request
is rejected. Accepted plan/hash bytes and exact error/bound distinctions must
remain equal. Retained per-map ordering references on invalid nested inputs
can cost depth times a per-map count bound even though final accepted values
are bounded; this is finite, not a zero-allocation or linear-work guarantee.

error/state fields. Large overwritten bytes therefore incur avoidable work.

plus supplied replacements after every guard, with no mutation of authority.

all exact source/lease/fence/history/atomic rollback tests. Boilerplate omissions,
public API changes, canonical equality weakening and broad boxing are rejected.
Existing checked resource charging bounds today's copy path; it does not prove

identical within each comparison and state it in output. Print raw samples,

**Primitive admission and owner sequence.** admit_case checks the next count
before runtime_header constructs the raw row. runtime_header validates native
map/tags shape, atom names, bounded file/root binaries and positive u64 line
before path/header conversions. Atom-to-string operations are VM-bounded;
the conservative raw header reservation is not an escaped whole-row bound.
The subsequent primitive scan supplies the latter before full normalization.

scan checks depth, prospective visit/container count, scalar lengths and
supported primitive kinds. Tuple-to-list conversion follows tuple_size/count
admission. Map keys reject unsupported kinds/collisions before normalization;
no arbitrary inspect/String.Chars protocol formats a key or callback. Invalid
UTF-8 binary values premeasure padded base64 plus the 20-byte wrapper and its
depth/visits before Base.encode64. Integer range checks precede JSON numeric
encoding. Normalization and external_size are additional bounded passes, with
one independently bounded candidate coexisting before retention. This is not
zero allocation or native-memory admission.

The budget stores cumulative runtime count, scanner visits and actual returned
external_size estimates. retain keeps intake :row separate from whole :index,
:container and :root roles. cons charges the singleton full head rather than
the growing prefix, under the reviewed previously owned-tail precondition.
The collector starts charged empty tails; completed owners, grouping buckets,
singleton index fragments, membership indexes, permutations and final roots
receive their separate logical charges. It does not repeatedly walk a growing
bucket or normalize a whole corpus through the 16 MiB intake API.

Actual complete/ sort expressions reserve a full-source occurrence before the
permutation, then assert the output external_size equals that reservation.
They retain the repeated scan cost explicitly. For a minimal five-field raw
row with file/line tags, direct admission needs at least 15 visits, singleton
cons at least 17, each complete-list scan 16*n+1. The current raw pipeline's
two complete charges plus sort charge therefore need at least 80*n+3 visits,
before empty owners and all other collector work. At 100,000 that lower bound
is 8,000,003, exceeding the four-million scanner profile. This strengthens,
without withdrawing, the earlier >=48*n+1 lower-bound qualification.

Primary upstream learning actually read during this phase:
[Vec try_reserve](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.try_reserve)
can grow beyond the requested minimum and reports allocator/overflow failure;
[BTreeSet insert](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.BTreeSet.html#method.insert)
keeps an existing equal entry and returns the new-entry boolean. These support
the source owner/order proof, not exact capacity or comparator timings.
[Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/marker/trait.Copy.html) duplicates bits of
borrowed/scalar fields; shared references qualify even when their referents do

P-ACT1: current workflow/batch.rs::build_plan reads every item from the original
canonical map, ordinary admission rejects repeated IDs, and each TransitionPlan
owns at most one history entry. Calling that API repeatedly cannot supply a
sequential closure with one shared budget and original expected versions. The
proposed bounded scalar/reference trace and one final owned record per touched
identity are the appropriate direction, subject to exact new body/owner proof.
All intermediate versions/events, source call order, original expected versions,
next ordinal and discarded operational failure must remain visible. Detect
cycles on the active dependency path without treating legal repeated roots or
shared already-resolved parents as cycles. Admitted missing dependencies require
complete canonical absence; a partial loaded relation map cannot prove a no-op.

P-ACT2: independently confirmed the owner's unscheduled FIFO observation.
select::read_heads validates and consumes the actual first member, but only
pushes a due candidate when DueOrder::for_record returns Some. Thus a nonterminal
next=None head still blocks followers. claim::apply::guard_consumed currently
requires that due unconditionally, and workflow::indexed::rows also evaluates
the due before either mode. A new timeout delta must represent FIFO membership
independently of optional head due; it must not manufacture a deadline or skip
a live head. The narrow proposed consumed-guard fix leaves existing full value
equality and D/name/G charges in place. This head has consumed/head work even
when it yields no selected record/P/F/T copy. This is an inspected composition
gap, not a runtime RED or newly executed source case.

P-ACT3: the proposed copied-owner equation needs one explicit clarification
before acceptance. R_u/A_u describe the initial final-record clone and replacement
bytes inserted into that owner; H_e describes history owners and O_j release
owners. A separate timeout value-write also owns a versioned partition/ID
identity. Those additional byte occurrences and its fixed descriptor must be
enumerated explicitly, either in a distinct value-write sum/count or in an
unambiguously broadened named existing term. "As appropriate" is insufficient
to count record error-ref, history error-ref and separate value-write identity
coexisting without double omissions. The typed error body is scalar; physical
encoded value bytes/reference availability remain outer gates. No ClaimPhase
4x budget or native size_of value automatically covers these new owners.

P-ACT4: require exact borrowed getter/delta signatures. Borrowed after-key rows
should be derived when accessing final writes, as current IndexedBatchPlan::deltas
does, with a lifetime tied to the borrow of the plan. They must not be stored as
self-references beside the vector that owns those same records. Original before/
delete keys may borrow original authority, with both owners alive through use.
record(view,id) and fifo_head must return borrows valid for the shorter plan/view
use, without retaining the roots argument. fifo_head(view,lane,work) currently
names only a profile: specify an explicit cumulative accumulator or admitted
charge result before claiming repeated calls share G. A profile supplied anew
does not establish aggregate work across parent phases. All removed-prefix rows,
surviving original head and compared changed members need before-comparison
length/authority/occurrence admission, including an unscheduled survivor.

The count/byte ordering in D-M1-A1 is otherwise an appropriate contract: raw
root counts before keys/lookup, actual consumed owner/group/ref counts and lengths
before full equality/enumeration, each repeated scalar visit including empty/
missing rows, and checked trace-derived P plus G before variable materialization.
An extra normalization/validation/refetch pass must be charged, even if it reads
already borrowed bytes. Current full canonical equality is retained; ID/version
alone cannot replace it. Group/member/key ordering and repeated long-prefix
BTree comparisons remain outside a literal CPU certificate. Count limits do
not bound the original maps' retained memory or prove adapter completeness.

The defaults are NEW trusted operation profiles, not source descendant limits:
100,000 visits/steps/links/deletions and 128 MiB represented work, with a separate
AdmissionLimits touched/output count and 16 MiB default copied-plan budget.
For arithmetic only, 100,000 visits plus 100,000 steps already consume
204,800,000 bytes = 195.3125 MiB of their 1,024-per-occurrence charges, before
group/link bytes or P. Therefore all count maxima cannot be simultaneously
reached under the default work cap. This is no source feasibility failure when
sufficient reviewed profiles remain available; tests must distinguish each cap,
exact/+1 boundaries, zero-byte occurrence work and cumulative multi-root refusal.
There is no timing, allocator or native-memory result in this observation.

Concrete optimization direction before any new artifact: freeze scalar steps
and source snapshots first; materialize one final touched record and clone each
parent group at most once, carrying per-event small fields/references separately.
Current lifecycle mutators call record.clone before overwriting lease/state/
error and changed_plan clones history state/worker. Chaining those existing
mutators per event would duplicate unrelated owned payload/group bytes and may
retain intermediate plans. A new trace materializer should avoid those copies
where the exact source events can still be described. It must count all actual
replacement/transient owners, not merely subtract strings that are later freed.
No blanket Box conversion, shared mutable Arc core, global group clone or
address-based canonical shortcut is proposed. Exact model/helper names remain
the domain's architecture consultation, and a later actual body review must
verify this opportunity rather than infer a measured gain now.

Primary official documentation actually read online in this phase:
[BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.BTreeMap.html)
provides borrowed lookup and ordered iteration; its node search can make
multiple comparisons, so one represented lookup is not one byte comparison.
The map's ordinary insertion interface does not promise a fallible capacity
reservation. [Vec try_reserve](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.try_reserve)
reports allocation/overflow failure and can reserve beyond the requested minimum;
bounded scalar/output vectors do not establish exact allocator consumption.
[Clone and clone_from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/clone/trait.Clone.html#method.clone_from)
describe per-field derived cloning and possible resource reuse, not a guaranteed
elimination of unrelated field copies. These primary APIs support ownership
reasoning, not workspace-version-specific native timing or a capacity profile.

### Primary guidance and concrete optimization limits

Actually reread official Rust1.99 online collection guidance. `try_reserve`
can grow speculatively and preserves contents on failure; `try_reserve_exact`
avoids deliberate over-reservation but allocator excess remains possible.
Current fallible quota/refund reservations therefore do not certify exact
native P bytes. [Vec reservation documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.try_reserve_exact)
supports this qualification. Tree insert/contains use ordered comparisons and
offer no recoverable allocation result; bounded rows/leaves do not make these
host allocations fallible. [BTreeSet API](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.BTreeSet.html#method.insert)
and [BTreeMap background/get](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.BTreeMap.html#method.get)
also support counting byte-prefix comparisons separately from logical K.
No native tree-node byte count follows from64*R/U/S.

The implemented constructor-only uniqueness avoids a SECOND reserved-ID set
while retaining current re-admission; this is a concrete eliminated owner,
not a measured throughput/RSS gain. Keeping mutable scalar quotas and borrowed
refund spines as Vec is coherent. [Box ownership documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/boxed/index.html)
provides no general replacement or speed argument; historical Darwin E1
conversion costs do not prove benefits for these distinct workloads.

One bounded FUTURE candidate is KnownNoCommit's known output count R<=1000:
after unchanged P+G admission, a single fallible reserve of R could replace
per-ID reserve calls while preserving original borrowed ID order. Current

latency is measured. Any owner edit/experiment needs separate exact architecture
consultation/root order and equivalence/failure checks. Accepted membership
cannot silently add a sizing traversal or worst-case reservation as the same

#### Trait, macro, ownership and diagnostic consequences

The existing LimitEnforcement at releases.rs11 derives Clone/Copy/Eq/PartialEq
and lacks Debug. Option<LimitEnforcement> therefore still makes assert_eq!'s
failure path require the missing trait, even when the expected value is None.
The inspected Rust1.99 assert_eq! macro borrows both operands and invokes
assert_failed, whose generic bounds require Debug. Boolean assert! avoids that
value-rendering requirement. Both macros enforce checks in debug and release;
default panic diagnostics differ. These are primary-document and SOURCE facts,
not an observed compiler RED or executed fix. See the official
[assert_eq! source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/src/core/macros/mod.rs.html#43-56),
[assert_failed bounds](https://doc.rust-lang.org/src/core/panicking.rs.html#397-408),
[assert_eq! documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.assert_eq.html) and
[assert! documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.assert.html).

For the FOUR equality assertions, ordinary comparisons implicitly borrow their
operands; tuple fields/getters evaluate left to right once. The selected Copy
scalars, Option<Copy enforcement>, Option<u64> and Option<&[u8]> add no owned
leaf or retained reference spine. The existing borrowed unit still receives the
same byte equality check. No ownership lifetime is widened. See the official
[comparison rules](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/operator-expr.html#comparison-operators)
and [operand evaluation order](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions.html#evaluation-order-of-operands).

and [Option::is_none](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html#method.is_none).

  then move the original Input/Caller as selected. A reference does not own or

  before pointer observations. Neither a source move nor pointer equality
  measures heap copying, allocator calls, ABI/stack work or error/Drop cost.

  [Clone semantics](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/clone/trait.Clone.html).

- **Vec/Box tradeoff.** Vec retains capacity as well as length; into_boxed_slice
  consumes it and discards spare capacity. Rust guarantees no reallocation or
  element movement for Vec/Box-slice conversion when len==capacity. Do not assume
  that guarantee for spare-capacity vectors or infer a fixed ABI/RSS saving.
  Later evidence would need the actual lengths/capacities, conversion cost,
  allocator behavior and simultaneous owners. No Box conversion is selected.
  [Vec guarantees and conversion](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#guarantees),

  consuming finalize. Feeding the exact frozen field order directly can avoid
  constructing an intent-output Vec in that path; this is a source opportunity,
  pending actual body review. It proves no zero-buffer/copy/allocation property
  inside SHA and no speed benefit for many small updates. Record the effective

  runtime on aarch64/x86 and fall back to software. Add no backend override.

  assess end-to-end cost. Moving Drop outside timing by retaining outputs changes
